title: Exact solutions of hidden free fermion models
authors: Mingchen Zheng, Balázs Pozsgay, Shu Chen
abstract: Hidden-free-fermion (HFF) Hamiltonians exhibit free-fermion spectra despite lacking an explicit quadratic representation, yet their algebraic provenance and periodic-boundary behavior remain open questions. Here we establish that a broad class of HFF models arises from distinct Lax operator realizations of a twisted multistate Perk--Schultz \(R\) matrix. Its reflected degeneration generates a closed finite hierarchy of mutually commuting transfer matrices, whose functional relations determine the complete many-body spectrum. As a decisive example, we solve the inhomogeneous free-fermions-in-disguise (FFD) chain, which exhibits HFF, nested HFF, or interacting spectra, depending on its coupling. The homogeneous FFD chain with both one-wrap and periodic boundary conditions exhibits an emergent cubic finite-size gap while retaining the exact \(z=3/2\) bulk behavior. The construction extends to higher-state and face-type realizations, providing a common algebraic framework for coupling-dependent spectral organization and multiscale behavior in interacting quantum systems.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive algebraic framework for understanding Hidden Free Fermion (HFF) models, unifying previously disparate integrable systems. By relating these models to the degeneration of a specific R matrix, the authors derive functional relations that determine the exact many-body spectrum. This advances the understanding of spectral organization and boundary effects in strongly correlated quantum chains.
main_problem: The paper establishes a unified algebraic framework to understand Hidden Free Fermion (HFF) models, which exhibit free-fermion spectra without an explicit quadratic representation.
main_result: A broad class of HFF models is shown to arise from Lax operator realizations of a twisted multistate Perk--Schultz R matrix, providing a common description for various spectral regimes.
method: The authors utilize the Yang–Baxter equation, fusion techniques, and the analysis of reflected degenerations of the R matrix to derive functional relations for commuting transfer matrices.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Hidden Free Fermion (HFF) Hamiltonian, exemplified by the inhomogeneous free-fermions-in-disguise (FFD) chain. The analysis extends to face-type and general integrable chains.
key_observables: The many-body spectrum determined by the functional relations of the transfer matrices, and the existence of an emergent cubic finite-size gap coexisting with the exact z=3/2 bulk behavior.
important_parameters: Coupling constants ($h_j$), boundary conditions (open vs. periodic), and the size $N$ of the system.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the existence of an underlying integrable structure governed by the Perk–Schultz R matrix and its associated Lax operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate zero-root configurations for the FFD chain under both open and periodic boundary conditions, and compare rescaled finite-size gaps ($\Delta N$) across different system sizes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general algebraic origin of HFF models via the R matrix, then applying this to the FFD chain to analyze spectral organization and boundary effects, and finally generalizing the framework to include face-type and other integrable chains.
why_interesting: The deep connection between algebraic integrability (R-matrices, Yang-Baxter equations) and the emergence of simple, solvable spectra (free fermions) in complex interacting models is highly relevant for understanding quantum many-body physics in condensed matter systems.
